summary: I found no stock-specific news that changes the research behind the research target (12m): the 2.2% drop on Nov 5 came on a day when the Nasdaq and chip stocks fell sharply, and I found no company-specific reason for it. The only new company item is an 8-K filed after the close on Nov 5 (items 8.01 and 9.01, which on EDGAR usually means financing paperwork); I could not open it, so its content is unverified, and it follows the euro bond sale already priced on Nov 2. No thesis trigger (guidance change, M&A, CEO exit, a search or appeal ruling, a large Cloud contract win or loss, or a dated catalyst moving) was found, and no Cloud deal, antitrust ruling, analyst action or data-centre policy item dated Nov 4-5 turned up.

items.headline: Alphabet Form 8-K filed 4:10pm ET (accession 0001193125-26-449835), items 8.01 (other events) and 9.01 (exhibits); main document about 1 MB
items.why: The filing's existence, date and item numbers are confirmed from the EDGAR filing list, but its text could not be opened (www.sec.gov blocks automated fetches and I did not try to get around that), so its content is unverified (fetch budget / access). The item codes and size fit debt-offering paperwork after the Nov 2 euro bond sale, which funds cash burn the research already expects; if it turns out to be something else, the next refresh should read it.

items.headline: Alphabet Form 424B2 prospectus supplement filed (matches the EUR 6 billion euro bond priced Nov 2)
items.why: Financing for the capex and cash burn the agents already model (Q3 free cash flow was negative); no new facts on cash flows. Filing confirmed from the EDGAR list; the document itself was not opened.

items.headline: Google to spend USD 15 billion on data-centre expansion in Malaysia over two years
items.why: Reported on Nov 4 (carried forward from the Nov 4 check; I did not re-open it). A multi-year build inside the existing capex path of about 301 billion for 2027 in the research; it supports, not breaks, the Cloud backlog conversion assumption.

items.headline: Nasdaq and chip stocks sell off sharply; GOOGL closes 282.57, down 2.2%
items.why: Price-move story: GOOGL fell far less than the Nasdaq (about 5.5%) and semis (about 12%) per the task context. Searches returned no Alphabet-specific cause and I could not confirm the date of the search-result articles on the index move. A price move alone is never a trigger.
